t: You are on Paternoster Row, a street in the City of London that was once the centre of the publishing trade. Booksellers worked from here, and the name was almost synonymous with the book trade. It lay within St Paul's Churchyard, and the name came to cover the alleys, courts and side streets around it. Bombing in the Second World War largely destroyed it, and the area is now part of the Paternoster Square development. Among those who lived here were Anne Turner, convicted in the 1613 poisoning of Sir Thomas Overbury, and Dick Sheppard, an Anglican priest and Christian pacifist who became Dean of Canterbury.
